claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances put this trip over the deviation tolerance: 11.4 km actually driven against a 10.0 km recommended route, a deviation of 1.40 km and 14.0% above the optimal route. POL-RD-22 sets the measure as trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km and treats a deviation of 1.0 km or less as within tolerance; 1.40 km is over it, so the reroute must be adjudicated on the refund matrix and cannot be waved away as a rounding-level detour. The platform's event log places the departure at the CTE / Bendemeer Road exit at 19:00:36 and the rejoin at Upper Serangoon Road / Braddell Road at 19:11:06, so the excess distance sits on the segment the rider is disputing.

The GPS trace's 9.652 km must not be used to shrink that 1.40 km. POL-RD-22 says in terms that the trace shows which route was taken and when and is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length; the trace here is 47 fixes at 30 s intervals with a 120 s gap ceiling, consistent with that warning. The route the trace does show — CTE to the Bendemeer Road exit, then Bendemeer Road and Upper Serangoon Road, rejoining only at 19:11:06 — is the route the deviation events describe.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record. The only traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-05003-01, is an ACCIDENT advisory for CTE towards SLE 'after Balestier Road exit', and its own derived block returns intersects_route as null, marks the question 'on the recommended route' as undetermined, and states that the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route. POL-RD-23 permits a reroute only where the traffic data shows congestion, an incident or a closure for the recommended route segment, and it adds that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. An advisory whose intersection with the recommended route is undetermined, and which the driver's own message is the only thing tying to that route, does not discharge that condition.

Even reading the chat log at its highest — the driver's 18:57:46 message warning of the CTE accident and proposing the Bendemeer Road exit, and the rider's 18:58:26 reply 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' — agreement is not a substitute for justification. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the reroute to be traffic-justified AND the rider informed AND agreed; the first condition is independent and, on this record, unmet. POL-RD-21's acknowledgment limb operates only on a reroute that is otherwise permitted, i.e. one made 'in response to real-time traffic, a road closure or congestion'. A rider's courteous assent to a driver's proposed exit cannot convert an unjustified detour into a justified one.

With the reroute not traffic-justified and the deviation over the 1 km tolerance, exactly one row of POL-RD-24's matrix applies: row (d), a refund of the excess distance fare in full. The arithmetic is fixed by the policy and the ledger: deviation 1.40 km x per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, without surge, = 1.008, rounded to the cent = 1.01 SGD. The fare ledger's own derived money block states excess_distance_fare_sgd of 1.01 SGD for this case. The present state is a metered fare of 22.60 SGD charged at 19:12:50 with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00; leaving that state standing under NO_ACTION would keep the rider carrying the excess distance charge, which is precisely what row (d) says must come back.

If the judge finds that the advisory's intersection with the recommended route cannot be established from this record at all, that is a fact POL-RD-23 needs and the record does not settle. POL-GEN-26 then requires the case to be escalated rather than resolved by inference from the absence of evidence. Escalation is the rider-favourable fallback here: the disputed amount is held for the human reviewer instead of the present charge being confirmed as final, whereas NO_ACTION would simply preserve the charge the rider is contesting.

claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances fix the deviation at 1.40 km — trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.4 km less trip_record.optimal_distance_km 10.0 km — which is above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22. The deviation is therefore a qualifying deviation, and the within-tolerance row of POL-RD-24 (row (c) or (e)) is closed on this record.

The driver discharged the notice obligation in POL-RD-21 before the point of deviation. He messaged the rider in-app at 18:57:46, delivered 18:57:48 and read 18:58:03 (MSG-05003-003), telling him of the CTE accident and that he would exit at Bendemeer; the platform does not record the route-deviation event until 19:00:36 at the CTE / Bendemeer Road exit. Notice therefore preceded the manoeuvre by roughly three minutes, and the reason given was more than the 'brief reason' the clause asks for.

The rider agreed. POL-RD-21 makes a chat-log acknowledgment conclusive — where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, the deviation is agreed — and here the rider replied at 18:58:26 (MSG-05003-004): 'Ok sure, thanks for telling.' That is an unqualified assent to the very reroute the driver proposed, given before the vehicle left the recommended route.

The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory LTA-TI-260805-1205 records an ACCIDENT — an admissible incident type under POL-RD-23's incident vocabulary — on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE at/after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, and its own derived block marks overlaps_trip_window true. The CTE is on the recommended route (Raffles Quay – CTE – Braddell Road – Upper Serangoon Road), the driver's contemporaneous message puts the jam 'after Balestier' ahead of him on that carriageway, and the platform records the deviation point itself on the CTE at the Bendemeer Road exit. The advisory artifact flags intersects_route as undetermined and leaves that question to the Judge; on the road, direction and platform-recorded deviation point, the driver's position is that it intersects.

On those three findings the case sits squarely in row (a) of POL-RD-24: the reroute was traffic-justified, the rider was informed and agreed, and the deviation exceeded 1 km. Row (a) pays no refund. The ruling is NO_ACTION and the metered fare of SGD 22.60 stands.

NO_ACTION is party-relative and the rider is the filer: the fare was charged (total_charged 22.60) and no refund has issued (refund_issued_sgd 0.0, payment_status CHARGED). Declining the rider's claim leaves the driver's payment exactly where it is, so NO_ACTION is the driver's outcome here.

A final AI ruling is available on this dispute. The contested amount is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; and POL-RD-25's 2 km condition does not bite, because thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false and the deviation is 1.40 km in any event. No escalation is required and the driver's defence should be decided on the merits.

The 4.50 SGD the rider asks for is not a figure the policy provides in any event. POL-RD-24 measures the excess distance fare as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 1.40 x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD. The rider's figure is inflated by the 1.3 surge_multiplier, which POL-RD-24 excludes, so even on the rider's own theory the contested sum overstates any recoverable amount several times over.

Row (a) turns on traffic justification, notice and agreement, not on whether the manoeuvre in fact saved seconds. The realised duration (23 min against a 20.2 min optimal) does not move the case out of row (a), and the traffic justification rests on the third-party LTA advisory, not on the driver's own assertion of speed.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides' claims turn on four facts, and the record settles them.

1. Deviation (POL-RD-22). The platform's own recorded distances are 11.4 km driven against a 10.0 km recommended route — a deviation of 1.40 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. Both parties agree on this and I accept it. The GPS trace's 9.652 km is not used to re-measure distance: POL-RD-22 says the trace shows which route was taken and when, not how long it was.

2. Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). EV-ADVIS-05003-01 (weight 1.0) records an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44 — overlapping the trip window (the trip ran 18:49:44 to 19:12:44). The recommended route runs Raffles Quay – CTE – Braddell Road – Upper Serangoon Road, i.e. northbound on the CTE past the Balestier Road exit and on to Braddell Road; the incident lies on that stretch of the recommended route and in the same direction of travel. The advisory's derived block expressly leaves the intersection question to the tribunal on road, direction and location against the trip, and on those it intersects. The reroute is therefore traffic-justified. The rider's submission that the intersection is undetermined and that only the driver's own message ties the advisory to the route is rejected: the route geometry ties it, independently of the message, so POL-GEN-26 does not arise and no escalation is required.

3. Notice and agreement (POL-RD-21). The driver messaged the rider in-app at 18:57:46 (delivered 18:57:48, read 18:58:03), explaining the CTE accident and proposing the Bendemeer Road exit; the rider replied at 18:58:26 'Ok sure, thanks for telling'. The platform's deviation event is recorded at 19:00:36. Notice therefore preceded the manoeuvre, and POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. The rider's separate argument that agreement cannot cure an unjustified reroute does not bite, because the reroute is justified.

4. Refund matrix (POL-RD-24). On those findings row (a) applies exactly — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — and row (a) pays no refund. The rider's row (d) claim fails for want of the 'not traffic-justified' condition. For completeness, the excess distance fare would in any event be 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.01 SGD, not the 4.50 SGD claimed, because POL-RD-24 excludes the 1.3 surge multiplier; that figure is not payable here. The realised duration (23 min against a 20.2 min optimal) does not move the case out of row (a).

Outcome and confidence. The contested amount is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so an AI ruling is final; POL-RD-25 requires confidence of 0.80, and every artifact carrying the deciding facts (EV-TRIP-05003, EV-CHAT-05003, EV-ADVIS-05003-01) carries weight 1.0. My confidence is 0.85. NO_ACTION means the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands — the metered fare of 22.60 SGD charged at 19:12:50, with nil refunded. No clause of the policy produces a referral on these facts.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties should read this. The SGD 22.60 metered fare charged for trip TRP-05003 stands; no refund is due.

To the rider: the detour you complained of did happen. The platform's recorded distances (EV-TRIP-05003) are 11.4 km driven against a 10.0 km recommended route, a deviation of 1.40 km, and 1.40 km is above the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so this is a qualifying deviation and not a rounding-level detour. Your fare is still not reduced, because POL-RD-24's refund matrix turns on two further questions and both go the driver's way. First, traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The LTA traffic record EV-ADVIS-05003-01 logs an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, overlapping your 18:49:44-19:12:44 trip; an ACCIDENT is an incident type POL-RD-23 accepts. Its derived block left to me whether it intersects the recommended route, and I decide it does: the CTE towards SLE is the corridor the recommended route follows (Raffles Quay - CTE - Braddell Road - Upper Serangoon Road), the Balestier Road exit lies on that stretch before the Braddell Road exit, and the platform places the deviation itself on the CTE at the Bendemeer Road exit at 19:00:36, at the incident. Second, notice and agreement (POL-RD-21). The driver messaged you in-app at 18:57:46, before the vehicle left the recommended route at 19:00:36, warning of the CTE accident after Balestier and asking whether he should exit at Bendemeer, and you replied at 18:58:26 'Ok sure, thanks for telling'; POL-RD-21 treats a chat-log acknowledgment as agreement to the deviation. Traffic-justified, rider informed, rider agreed, deviation over 1 km: that is row (a) of POL-RD-24, which pays no refund. Your figure of SGD 4.50 exceeds even the measure the policy provides: the excess distance fare is 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.01 SGD (the fare ledger EV-FARE-05003 states 1.01 SGD), POL-RD-24 excludes the 1.3 surge, and nothing is payable on row (a) in any event. I rejected the argument that POL-GEN-26 requires escalation: the evidence carrying the traffic fact is present and complete, not missing or impaired. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05003, 9.652 km) was not used to re-measure the distance, as POL-RD-22 requires, and the realised duration (23.0 min against 20.2 min optimal) does not decide the case.

To the driver: your account is accepted. The trip record, the LTA advisory and the chat log together establish that you rerouted for a real incident on the recommended route, told the rider first, and received his agreement, so the deviation is agreed under POL-RD-21 and no refund issues under row (a).

On who decides: the contested amount is SGD 4.50, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; POL-RD-25 requires a confidence of 0.80, every artifact carries weight 1.0 and none is impaired, and my confidence is 0.85, so the ruling stands. No clause produces a referral, and the referrals list is empty.

ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances put this trip over the deviation tolerance: 11.4 km actually driven against a 10.0 km recommended route, a deviation of 1.40 km and 14.0% above the optimal route. POL-RD-22 sets the measure as trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km and treats a deviation of 1.0 km or less as within tolerance; 1.40 km is over it, so the reroute must be adjudicated on the refund matrix and cannot be waved away as a rounding-level detour. The platform's event log places the departure at the CTE / Bendemeer Road exit at 19:00:36 and the rejoin at Upper Serangoon Road / Braddell Road at 19:11:06, so the excess distance sits on the segment the rider is disputing.

The GPS trace's 9.652 km must not be used to shrink that 1.40 km. POL-RD-22 says in terms that the trace shows which route was taken and when and is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length; the trace here is 47 fixes at 30 s intervals with a 120 s gap ceiling, consistent with that warning. The route the trace does show — CTE to the Bendemeer Road exit, then Bendemeer Road and Upper Serangoon Road, rejoining only at 19:11:06 — is the route the deviation events describe.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record. The only traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-05003-01, is an ACCIDENT advisory for CTE towards SLE 'after Balestier Road exit', and its own derived block returns intersects_route as null, marks the question 'on the recommended route' as undetermined, and states that the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route. POL-RD-23 permits a reroute only where the traffic data shows congestion, an incident or a closure for the recommended route segment, and it adds that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. An advisory whose intersection with the recommended route is undetermined, and which the driver's own message is the only thing tying to that route, does not discharge that condition.

Even reading the chat log at its highest — the driver's 18:57:46 message warning of the CTE accident and proposing the Bendemeer Road exit, and the rider's 18:58:26 reply 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' — agreement is not a substitute for justification. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the reroute to be traffic-justified AND the rider informed AND agreed; the first condition is independent and, on this record, unmet. POL-RD-21's acknowledgment limb operates only on a reroute that is otherwise permitted, i.e. one made 'in response to real-time traffic, a road closure or congestion'. A rider's courteous assent to a driver's proposed exit cannot convert an unjustified detour into a justified one.

With the reroute not traffic-justified and the deviation over the 1 km tolerance, exactly one row of POL-RD-24's matrix applies: row (d), a refund of the excess distance fare in full. The arithmetic is fixed by the policy and the ledger: deviation 1.40 km x per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, without surge, = 1.008, rounded to the cent = 1.01 SGD. The fare ledger's own derived money block states excess_distance_fare_sgd of 1.01 SGD for this case. The present state is a metered fare of 22.60 SGD charged at 19:12:50 with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00; leaving that state standing under NO_ACTION would keep the rider carrying the excess distance charge, which is precisely what row (d) says must come back.

If the judge finds that the advisory's intersection with the recommended route cannot be established from this record at all, that is a fact POL-RD-23 needs and the record does not settle. POL-GEN-26 then requires the case to be escalated rather than resolved by inference from the absence of evidence. Escalation is the rider-favourable fallback here: the disputed amount is held for the human reviewer instead of the present charge being confirmed as final, whereas NO_ACTION would simply preserve the charge the rider is contesting.

The platform's own recorded distances fix the deviation at 1.40 km — trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.4 km less trip_record.optimal_distance_km 10.0 km — which is above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22. The deviation is therefore a qualifying deviation, and the within-tolerance row of POL-RD-24 (row (c) or (e)) is closed on this record.

The driver discharged the notice obligation in POL-RD-21 before the point of deviation. He messaged the rider in-app at 18:57:46, delivered 18:57:48 and read 18:58:03 (MSG-05003-003), telling him of the CTE accident and that he would exit at Bendemeer; the platform does not record the route-deviation event until 19:00:36 at the CTE / Bendemeer Road exit. Notice therefore preceded the manoeuvre by roughly three minutes, and the reason given was more than the 'brief reason' the clause asks for.

The rider agreed. POL-RD-21 makes a chat-log acknowledgment conclusive — where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, the deviation is agreed — and here the rider replied at 18:58:26 (MSG-05003-004): 'Ok sure, thanks for telling.' That is an unqualified assent to the very reroute the driver proposed, given before the vehicle left the recommended route.

The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory LTA-TI-260805-1205 records an ACCIDENT — an admissible incident type under POL-RD-23's incident vocabulary — on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE at/after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, and its own derived block marks overlaps_trip_window true. The CTE is on the recommended route (Raffles Quay – CTE – Braddell Road – Upper Serangoon Road), the driver's contemporaneous message puts the jam 'after Balestier' ahead of him on that carriageway, and the platform records the deviation point itself on the CTE at the Bendemeer Road exit. The advisory artifact flags intersects_route as undetermined and leaves that question to the Judge; on the road, direction and platform-recorded deviation point, the driver's position is that it intersects.

On those three findings the case sits squarely in row (a) of POL-RD-24: the reroute was traffic-justified, the rider was informed and agreed, and the deviation exceeded 1 km. Row (a) pays no refund. The ruling is NO_ACTION and the metered fare of SGD 22.60 stands.

NO_ACTION is party-relative and the rider is the filer: the fare was charged (total_charged 22.60) and no refund has issued (refund_issued_sgd 0.0, payment_status CHARGED). Declining the rider's claim leaves the driver's payment exactly where it is, so NO_ACTION is the driver's outcome here.

A final AI ruling is available on this dispute. The contested amount is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; and POL-RD-25's 2 km condition does not bite, because thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false and the deviation is 1.40 km in any event. No escalation is required and the driver's defence should be decided on the merits.

The 4.50 SGD the rider asks for is not a figure the policy provides in any event. POL-RD-24 measures the excess distance fare as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 1.40 x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD. The rider's figure is inflated by the 1.3 surge_multiplier, which POL-RD-24 excludes, so even on the rider's own theory the contested sum overstates any recoverable amount several times over.

Row (a) turns on traffic justification, notice and agreement, not on whether the manoeuvre in fact saved seconds. The realised duration (23 min against a 20.2 min optimal) does not move the case out of row (a), and the traffic justification rests on the third-party LTA advisory, not on the driver's own assertion of speed.
